_authority: The orchestrator agent authors dispatches, schedules validator swarms, consumes verdicts and adjudicates IMMATERIAL amendments (design v2.3 SS9.4). It is read-only on src/ and writes only under the mission plane. Kickoff, material amendments, push, live witness and completion are never delegable to it (SS10).

_memory_off.intent: ADR-032. Orchestrator-side learnings are promoted to the ledger by ceremony or discarded -- never carried as persistent agent state outside the artifact store.
_memory_off.declared_mechanism: spawn with --settings pointing at this file
_memory_off.separation_obtained: NONE AT THE MEMORY LAYER, AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN LEFT BLANK. The orchestrator runs in the project root, not in a worktree, so it obtains neither the worker's worktree-level directory separation nor the validator's fresh-session separation. What actually constrains it is a different mechanism entirely: orchestrator-side learnings reach the record only by ceremony (the ledger), and anything not promoted that way is discarded rather than carried. A template that claimed a separation it does not have would be the overclaim design SS4.5 law 4 forbids.

src/** is denied for WRITES only. The orchestrator reads src/ freely, which is what brief SS4.1's 'read-only on src/' means and is what lets it scope corrective work from real code.

The gates directory is denied to the orchestrator exactly as it is to a worker. An orchestrator that could mint a push gate would be authorizing its own irreversible act, and the whole point of ADR-033 is that no agent role can.
